Chapter 11: Human Connections—Between Nearness and Distance
You know, even though we’ve got more ways to connect than ever before, a lot of people still feel lonely. Imagine sitting in a busy café—there’s a woman scrolling through her phone, checking out what everyone’s up to online, but deep down, she feels miles away from them all.
One day, she decides to do something different—she calls up an old friend and invites her to meet in person. They sit together, reminiscing about the past, sharing dreams, and laughing until their cheeks hurt. That’s when she realizes something powerful: real closeness isn’t about how many messages or likes you get, but those honest, warm moments you actually share with someone.
There’s another story—a man meets a new coworker. At first, he feels a bit awkward and reserved. But as time passes, he discovers they have a lot in common, and that open, honest conversations can break down walls and spark genuine understanding. It turns out, building human relationships takes time and effort—they can’t really grow in a vacuum or just through screens.
A lot of us think strong relationships just happen naturally, but the truth is, every connection needs care. Every time you choose to be real, to listen without judging, or to share your feelings clearly, you’re taking a step closer to building something real.
As time goes on, it becomes clear: being close or distant isn’t really about geography—it’s about what’s in your heart. In the end, human relationships are our true safe haven when life gets tough. They’re the biggest source of joy, support, and hope we have.
